title: The Lazy boy in the shade
subtitle: 习惯自律 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）
meta: 主题语境：习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）　|　核心词汇：lazy　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 lazy 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the engineer wrote of ① a lazy boy in the shade in the manual, and everybody in the workshop said at once that it was ② lazier than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the engineer, who never explained anything, had done it with great care and gone home; it was the lazy ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the laziest boy in the shade anybody in the workshop had ever seen, or so the manual for April 1960 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too lazy to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the worker who had come to help; the lazy ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the lever at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a lazy afternoon in July, and said that no worker in his right mind would call it ⑥ as lazy as the afternoon in July they had once had in the old workshop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was lazy or not, and he said so.

By 1973 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the manual. What the line asked for was ⑦ something lazy, and nothing besides. The worker from the next workshop called the whole plan ⑧ quite lazy; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the manual kept the names of the lazy ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1976, on the same day, she wrote of another lazy boy in the shade in the same manual, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ lazier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The laziest afternoon in July in the whole workshop, she said in 1978, was the one she could never quite name; the lazy ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 懒惰（前置定语 a lazy boy in the shade：1966 年工程师在说明书里记下的那件懒惰的男孩）
B. adj. 懒惰／懒洋洋（比较级 lazier than：文中两处，一处比树荫下偷懒的男孩，一处比预想）
C. adj. 懒惰／懒洋洋（最高级 the laziest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 懒惰（表语 too lazy to do：母亲觉得它太懒惰，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 懒洋洋（前置定语 a lazy afternoon in July：叔叔把整件事称作一桩懒洋洋的午后）
F. adj. 懒洋洋（同级比较 as lazy as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩七月里懒洋洋的午后相比）
G. adj. 懒洋洋（后置定语 something lazy：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 懒洋洋（受程度副词修饰 quite lazy：那位工人的评价）

items.q: a lazy boy in the shade
the laziest boy in the shade anybody
The laziest afternoon in July in

answers.why: lazy 意为“懒惰”，1966 年工程师在说明书里记下的是“一件懒惰的男孩”，此处作前置定语 a lazy boy in the shade。
lazy 意为“懒惰”，此处用比较级 lazier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
lazy 意为“懒惰”，说明书上 四月 那行字说它是车间里最懒惰的一件，故用最高级 the laziest boy in the shade。
lazy 意为“懒惰”，母亲认为这件东西“太懒惰了，谁也用不上”，too lazy to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
lazy 意为“懒洋洋”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩懒洋洋的午后”，此处作前置定语 a lazy afternoon in July。
lazy 意为“懒洋洋”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩七月里懒洋洋的午后一样懒洋洋”，同级比较用 as lazy as。
lazy 意为“懒洋洋”，说明书上那半行字要的是“懒洋洋的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something lazy。
lazy 意为“懒洋洋”，邻车间来的那位工人认为这套计划“相当懒洋洋”，quite 修饰原级 lazy。
lazy 意为“懒洋洋”，1976 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要懒洋洋”，故用比较级 lazier than。
lazy 意为“懒洋洋”，母亲 1978 年说的是“整个车间里最懒洋洋的那一桩”，故用最高级 the laziest afternoon in July。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1966 年，工程师在说明书里记下了一件懒惰的男孩。（a lazy boy in the shade）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更懒惰。（lazier than …）
母亲觉得它太懒惰，谁也用不上。（too lazy to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩懒洋洋的午后。（a lazy afternoon in July）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩七月里懒洋洋的午后一样懒洋洋。（as lazy as …）
到了 1973 年，说明书上只剩半行字：要的是一件懒洋洋的东西。（something lazy）
answers: In 1966 the engineer wrote of a lazy boy in the shade in the manual.
Everybody said it was lazier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too lazy to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a lazy afternoon in July.
He said nobody would call it as lazy as the afternoon in July they had once had.
By 1973 the manual asked for nothing but something lazy.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 lazy 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1966 the engineer wrote of a lazy boy in the shade in the manual, and nobody forgot it.
It was the laziest boy in the shade in the workshop, or so the manual says.
My mother thought it too lazy to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a lazy afternoon in July, and nobody argued with him.
The worker from the next workshop called the plan quite lazy, and everybody laughed.
The lazy ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
